references.text: Abram believed the Lord, and it was credited to him as righteousness. This is the foundation for the idea that faith and obedience lead to righteousness.
Phinehas' action was credited to him as righteousness, a parallel to how obedience to the commands leads to righteousness.
Blessed are those who walk in the Lord's law and keep his commandments. This expresses the same thought of blessing through obedience.
Maintain justice and do what is right, for my salvation is near. The connection between keeping the commandments and righteousness is confirmed.
The righteous person who keeps the Lord's laws and commandments shall live. This emphasizes that obedience to the commands leads to life and righteousness.
Paul discusses how Abraham was credited with righteousness by faith, contrasting this with righteousness by works.
Moses writes about the righteousness that comes from the law: the one who does these things shall live by them. A direct reference to the righteousness of the law.
Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness. Paul uses this to explain the relationship between faith and righteousness.
Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac. James shows that faith and works go together for righteousness.
